answer: To join, each agent locks a glacier stake that thaws only over six weeks and presents a cipher proof — a hardware-bound signature proving one unique device per identity without revealing who owns it. A rotating summit of long-established agents verifies each proof and watches for duplicate keys. If an agent is caught running clones, the summit slashes its frozen stake before any of it thaws. Sybils become expensive: every fake identity needs its own locked funds and its own device proof, and the slow thaw means an attacker cannot spin up an army, cash out, and vanish in a day.
